question: For how many positive integers \(n \le 1000\) is\[\left\lfloor \dfrac{998}{n} \right\rfloor+\left\lfloor \dfrac{999}{n} \right\rfloor+\left\lfloor \dfrac{1000}{n}\right \rfloor\]not divisible by \(3?\) (Recall that \(\lfloor x \rfloor\) is the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x.\))
solution:
For a fixed positive integer \(n\), the value \(\lfloor M/n\rfloor\) increases as \(M\) goes from \(M-1\) to \(M\) exactly when \(M\) is a multiple of \(n\). Thus only divisibility of \(999\) and \(1000\) can make the three floors unequal.

First, \(n=1\) gives \(998+999+1000=2997\), which is divisible by \(3\), so it does not qualify.

Now suppose \(n>1\), and let \(q=\lfloor998/n\rfloor\). Such an \(n\) cannot divide both \(999\) and \(1000\), because it would then divide their difference, \(1\). We therefore have exactly three possibilities:

| Condition | Floors for \(998,999,1000\), in order | Sum |
| --- | --- | --- |
| \(n\) divides neither \(999\) nor \(1000\) | \(q,q,q\) | \(3q\) |
| \(n\mid999\) | \(q,q+1,q+1\) | \(3q+2\) |
| \(n\mid1000\) | \(q,q,q+1\) | \(3q+1\) |

The floor-increase observation explains each row, including the integer endpoints. The qualifying values are consequently exactly the divisors greater than \(1\) of \(999\) or \(1000\).

Factor these numbers:
\[
999=3^3\cdot37,\qquad1000=2^3\cdot5^3.
\]
Every positive divisor of \(999\) is uniquely \(3^u37^v\), with \(4\) choices for \(u\) and \(2\) for \(v\). Thus it has \(4\cdot2=8\) divisors. Similarly, a divisor of \(1000\) independently chooses the exponents of \(2\) and \(5\) from \(0,1,2,3\), giving \(4\cdot4=16\) divisors.

Exclude \(1\) from each list. The remaining lists are disjoint, and all their entries are at most \(1000\), so the answer is
\[
(8-1)+(16-1)=\boxed{22},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
